title: Fourth-order invariance principle
statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let $F$ be a multilinear polynomial on $\{0,1\}^n$ of degree at most $k$, written in the Walsh basis as $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\chi_S(x)$. Let $X_i\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y_i\colon\Xi\to\mathbb R$ be independent families under probability measures $\mu$ and $\nu$, respectively. Suppose every input has mean zero, second moment one, third moment zero, finite fourth moment, and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is four times continuously differentiable, $C\ge0$, and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, then
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\mu\psi\!\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i\right)-\mathbb E_\nu\psi\!\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}Y_i\right)\right|
\le \frac C{12}9^k\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^2,
\]
where $\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]$ is the uniform-cube expectation of $(F(x)-F(x^i))^2/4$, with $x^i$ obtained by flipping coordinate $i$.
hypotheses_covered: The underlying spaces are measurable and $\mu,\nu$ are probability measures
The coordinate inputs form independent families under their respective measures
Each input satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions: mean $0$, second moment $1$, third moment $0$, and fourth moment at most $9$
